#### [kaggle_cli.download](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) Function {#func.kaggle_cli.download}
\

Automates downloading datasets directly from [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets) into a specified local directory using the [Kaggle command-line interface* (*CLI*)](https://github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli/blob/main/docs/datasets.md#kaggle-datasets-download).

\newpage

::: { #func.kaggle_cli.download.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/ds.kaggle.download.R#L16)
\

```{r kaggle_cli.download@usage.setup, include=FALSE}
open_logfile(".report.appx_a.kaggle_cli.download")
path <- file.path(knitr.proj_root, raw_data.chars.dir)

```
```{r kaggle_cli.download@usage, eval=FALSE}
kaggle_dataset <- "vaibhao/handwritten-characters"

  put_log("Downloading dataset `%1` ...", kaggle_dataset)
  kaggle_cli.download(kaggle_dataset, raw_data.chars.dir, unzip = TRUE)
```  
```{r kaggle_cli.download@usage.result, echo=FALSE}
  
  put_log("The Kaggle image files have been downloaded 
and unziped to the following directory: 
`%1`", path)

writeLines("*** Dataset Raw Data Local Directory Structure ***")
dir_tree(path, type = 'directory')

```
```{r kaggle_cli.download@usage.finalize, include=FALSE}
rm(path)
log_close()
```

::: { #func.kaggle_cli.download.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.kaggle_cli.download.args.arg1 .sidebar }
- **dataset.dir:** *Remote path* to the [Kaggle dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets); 

:::
::: { #func.kaggle_cli.download.args.arg2 .sidebar }
- **data.local_path:** *Local directory path* where the dataset files are saved;

:::
::: { #func.kaggle_cli.download.args.arg5 .sidebar }
- **unzip:**  (Optional, *Boolean*, $FALSE$ by default) Logical flag indicating whether the *downloaded archive* should be automatically unzipped.
 

:::
:::

::: { #func.kaggle_cli.download.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. **Prerequisite Check:** Verifies that the [Kaggle CLI](https://github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli/blob/main/docs/datasets.md#kaggle-datasets-download) is installed and accessible in the system's PATH (by running the kaggle --version command).
2. **Download Operation:** Executes the CLI command `kaggle datasets download <kaggle_dataset> --path <path>` (with an optional `--unzip` flag if requested).
3. **Verification:** Checks that the local destination directory exists after the download completes, indicating that the download operation was successful.

:::

\newpage

::: { #func.kaggle_cli.download.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) of the function is shown below:
```{r kaggle_cli.download@source, eval=FALSE}
kaggle_cli.download <- function(dataset.dir, data.local_path, unzip = FALSE) {
  # Check for Kaggle CLI Installation
  if (system("kaggle --version", ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE) != 0) {
    #' Kaggle command-line interface is missing or not configured 
    #' in your system's PATH.
    stop("Kaggle CLI is not installed or not in the PATH.")
  }
  
  # Download the Dataset via CLI
  if (system(trimws(paste("kaggle datasets download", kaggle_dataset, "--path", 
                          data.local_path, ifelse(unzip, "--unzip", "")))) != 0) {
    stop(str.build("Failed to download the dataset with Kaggle CLI: `%1`.", dataset.dir))
  }
  
  #'Verify that the dataset’s local directory exists, 
  #'as it should have been created automatically during the download.
  if(!dir.exists(data.local_path)) {
    stop(str.build("Failed to download and unzip the Kaggle dataset: `%1`.", dataset.dir))
  }
}

```

\newpage

#### [load_image.list](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L80) Function {#func.load_image.list}
\

This is a core utility designed to recursively traverse a root directory passed in the [root_path](#func.load_image.list.args.root_path) argument, discover character-specific (or class-specific, in the terms of the project's multiclass classifier models) subfolders, load data from raw image files (downloaded from the [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vaibhao/handwritten-characters) platform) using a custom parsing function, the pointer to which is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument, filter out empty or invalid images, and organize everything into an `R` list object with the corresponding labels and file paths.

::: { #func.load_image.list.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/ds.train2trimmed_img.dat.R#L12)
\

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
In the *code snippet* below, a pointer to the auxiliary function [load.img_trimmed.dat](#func.load.img_trimmed.dat) described below in *this Section* is used as the value of the argument [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat).
:::

```{r load_image.list@usage.setup, include=FALSE}
path <- file.path(knitr.proj_root, train.img_dat.list.file)
stopifnot(file.exists(path))
train.img_dat.list <- readRDS(path)

```
```{r load_image.list@usage, eval=FALSE}
  put_log("Creating an Image list from the raw data files 
stored in the following root directory: %1,
Please wait...", img.train_root.dir)

  train.img_dat.list <- load_image.list(root_path = img.train_root.dir,
                                        fn.load_image.dat = load.img_trimmed.dat
                                        # folder.list = NULL,
                                        # char_files.max = NA,
                                        # seed = NA,
                                        # random_sample = FALSE
                                        )

```
```{r load_image.list@usage.img_data, echo=FALSE }
writeLines('*** Training Image Data List Structure ***')

print_log("Class Labels:
%1", capture.output(train.img_dat.list$label.list))


class_names <- names(train.img_dat.list$img.list)

for (class_name in class_names) {
  print_log("Class Name: %1", class_name)

  class_list <- train.img_dat.list$img.list[[class_name]]
  # print(names(class_list))
  
  
  img.list <- class_list$img.list
  
  # writeLines("*** Image Files Number: ***", sep = ' ')
  print_log("Image Files Number: %1", length(img.list))

  fpath.list <- class_list$fpath.list
  
  print_log("Image File Path example: 
%1", fpath.list[[1]])
  # cat(head(fpath.list), sep = '\n')
  
  writeLines("Image File Shape:")
  print(shape(img.list[[1]]))
  writeLines("")
}

```
```{r load_image.list@cleanup, include=FALSE}
rm(path,
   train.img_dat.list)
```

:::

\newpage

::: { #func.load_image.list.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.load_image.list.args.root_path .sidebar }
- **root_path:** The root directory path containing subfolders of images organized by character recognition classes; 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat .sidebar }
- **fn.load_image.dat:** Pointer to a user-defined loading and processing helper function applied to each image file path (e.g., a function to read image matrices or binary arrays); 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.folder.list .sidebar }
- **folder.list:**  (Optional, *Character*, `NULL` by default) Vector of specific subfolder names to process. If `NULL`, it defaults to all directories found inside the *root path* passed in the [root_path](#func.load_image.list.args.root_path) argument; 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.char_files.max .sidebar }
- **char_files.max:**  (Optional, *Integer*, `NA` by default) Numeric value limiting the maximum number of files to load per folder (useful for subsampling or testing); 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.seed .sidebar }
- **seed:**  (Optional, *Integer*, `NA` by default) Random seed used for reproducible sampling when [char_files.max](#func.load_image.list.args.char_files.max) is specified (ignored otherwise); 

:::
::: { #func.load_image.list.args.random_sample .sidebar }
- **random_sample:**  (Optional, *Boolean*, `FALSE` by default) Boolean (`TRUE/FALSE`) indicating whether files within a folder should be sampled randomly (`TRUE`) or taken sequentially from the top (`FALSE`). 

:::
:::

::: { #func.load_image.list.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. **File Path Discovery:** Internally invokes the [img.file_path.get_list](#func.img.file_path.get_list) user-defined helper function (described below in the [Image Processing](#appndx_a@img_proc) Section) to gather a structured list of file paths from each target subfolder, applying optional maximum limits (passed in the [char_files.max](#func.load_image.list.args.char_files.max) argument), random sampling (depending on the value passed in the [random_sample](#func.load_image.list.args.random_sample) argument), and seed generation (if the [seed](#func.load_image.list.args.seed) argument value is not `NA`).

2. **Label Generation:** Extracts directory names from the file path list and converts them into a factor to serve as classification labels.

3. **Iterative processing of class directories:** Iterates through each directory, performing the following operations:
    a) **Batch Loading:** Calls the custom loader function (the pointer to which is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument) using the [map](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/purrr/versions/1.2.0/topics/map) `R` function across all file paths in the folder.
    b) **Data Validation & Filtering:** Evaluates a validity check on the loaded image data. Specifically, it checks that the binary matrix elements sum to greater than zero, effectively filtering out blank, corrupt, or unreadable images.

4. **Consistency Checks:** Enforces a safety assertion to ensure that the filtered image list length strictly matches the corresponding filtered file path list length.

:::

::: { #func.load_image.list.value .sidebar }
##### Value
\

Structured list containing two primary components:

1. *Label list:* A factor of *class labels*;
2. *Image list:* A nested list mapping each *class folder* to its valid loaded *image data* and corresponding *file paths*.

:::

\newpage

::: { #func.load_image.list.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The simplified version of the function's source code is shown below:
```{r func@load_image.list.s, eval=FALSE}
load_image.list <- function(root_path,
                            fn.load_image.dat,
                            folder.list = NULL, 
                            char_files.max = NA,
                            seed = NA,
                            random_sample = FALSE) {
  #'Gather a structured list of file paths from each target subfolder, 
  #'applying optional maximum limits, random sampling, and seed generation. 
  img.file_list <- img.file_path.get_list(root_path, 
                                          folder.list,
                                          char_files.max,
                                          seed,
                                          random_sample)

  #' Extracts directory names from the file path list 
  #' and converts them into a factor to serve as classification labels.
  label_list <- as.factor(names(img.file_list))
  
  # Load structured image data list
  img_list <- lapply(img.file_list, function(char.dir){

    #' Batch Loading using the custom loader function `fn.load_image.dat`.
    img_dat.ls <- map(char.dir$file_path.list, 
                  fn.load_image.dat)
    
    # Evaluates a validity check on the loaded image data. 
    valid.idx <- sapply(img_dat.ls, function(img.dat){
      mx.bin <- img.dat[1,,]
      mode(mx.bin) <- "numeric"
      
      # Filter out blank, corrupt, or unreadable images.
      sum(mx.bin) > 0
    })
    
    ls <- list(img.list = img_dat.ls[valid.idx], 
               fpath.list = char.dir$file_path.list[valid.idx])
    
    #' Ensures that the filtered image list length strictly matches 
    #' the corresponding filtered file path list length.
    stopifnot(length(ls$img.list) == length(ls$fpath.list))
    
    ls
  })
  
  list(label.list = label_list,
       img.list = img_list)
}
```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
The complete version of the [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L80) is available in the [Data Loading](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L-L) Section of the [data.helper.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) script on _GitHub_.
:::
:::

#### [img.file_path.get_list](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L421) Function {#func.img.file_path.get_list}
\

This function traverses *image directories*, collects *file paths* grouped by *folder* (representing *class labels*), and optionally limits, seeds, or randomly samples files for *dataset preparation*.

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L)
\

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
In the *code snippet* below, *this function* is called internally from the [load_image.list](#func.load_image.list) function described above in *this Section*.
:::
:::

``` {r img.file_path.get_list@usage.setup, include=FALSE}
open_logfile(".chunk.img.file_path.get_list@usage")
root_path <- file.path(knitr.proj_root, img.train_root.dir)
# dir(root_path)
```
``` {r img.file_path.get_list@usage_log, echo=TRUE}

put_log("Function `load_image.list`:
Getting file path lists from the following Root Path:
%1", root_path)

folder.list <- NULL 
char_files.max <- NA
seed <- NA
random_sample <- FALSE


#'Gather a structured list of file paths from each target subfolder, 
#'applying optional maximum limits, random sampling, and seed generation. 
img.file_list <- img.file_path.get_list(root_path, 
                                        folder.list,
                                        char_files.max,
                                        seed,
                                        random_sample)

```
``` {r img.file_path.get_list@usage_cleanup, include=FALSE}
rm(root_path,
   char_files.max,
   seed,
   random_sample)
log_close()
```

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.root_path .sidebar }
- **root_path:** The root directory path containing subfolders of images organized by character recognition classes; 

:::
::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.folder.list .sidebar }
- **folder.list:**  (Optional, *Character*, `NULL` by default) Vector of specific subfolder names to process. If `NULL`, it defaults to all directories found inside the *root path* passed in the [root_path](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.root_path) argument; 

:::
::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.char_files.max .sidebar }
- **char_files.max:**  (Optional, *Integer*, `NA` by default) Numeric value limiting the maximum number of files to list per folder (useful for subsampling or testing); 

:::
::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.seed .sidebar }
- **seed:**  (Optional, *Integer*, `NA` by default) Random seed used for reproducible sampling when [char_files.max](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.char_files.max) is specified (ignored otherwise); 

:::
::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.args.random_sample .sidebar }
- **random_sample:**  (Optional, *Boolean*, `FALSE` by default) Logical ($TRUE / FALSE$) value indicating whether files within a folder should be sampled randomly (`TRUE`) or taken sequentially from the top (`FALSE`). 

:::
:::

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

This is an auxiliary function that is used internally in the [load_image.list](#func.load_image.list) function as shown above in the [Usage](#func.img.file_path.get_list.usage) Section of *this Description*.

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. **Subfolder Discovery:** If the [folder.list](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.folder.list) argument value is `NULL` (the *folder list* is not provided), the function retrieves all subdirectory names inside the *root directory* (using the path passed in the [root_path](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.root_path) argument) and uses them as the *folder list* for further processing. Otherwise, the [folder.list](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.folder.list) value is used.
2. **File Path Collection:** Next, it iterates through the *folder list* determined in the previous step, constructs the *full path* for each folder, and retrieves all file paths in that folder.
3. **Capping and Sampling:** If the value for the [char_files.max](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.char_files.max) argument is provided and does not exceed the folder's file count, the number of files to process is limited to that value. 

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
- If the condition above is met, the *file selection method* depends on the value of the [random_sample](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.random_sample) argument. If it is `TRUE`, a *sample* of the size provided in the [char_files.max](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.char_files.max) argument is taken using a *reproducibility seed offset* by the folder's index if a *seed* is provided (the value of the [seed](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.seed) argument is not `NA`). Otherwise, a top list of the size provided in the [char_files.max](#func.img.file_path.get_list.args.char_files.max) argument is selected.
- Otherwise, the full list of file paths obtained in the previous step is used for the final result.

:::
:::

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.value .sidebar }
##### Value
\

A *named nested list* where each element represents a *subfolder*, containing its *root path* and the *file path list*.
:::

::: { #func.img.file_path.get_list.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The slightly simplified version of the function's source code is shown below:
```{r src@img.file_path.get_list, eval=FALSE}
img.file_path.get_list <- function(root_path, 
                                   folder.list = NULL, 
                                   char_files.max = NA,
                                   seed = NA,
                                   random_sample = FALSE) {
  if(is.null(folder.list))
    # Scans the root path to find all available subfolders.
    folder.list <- dir(root_path)

  # Generates a file path list
  path_list <- lapply(folder.list, function(folder_name){
    #' Constructs the full path and retrieves all file paths 
    #' for the given folder name.
    file.root_path <- file.path(root_path, folder_name)
    folder.idx <- which(folder.list == folder_name)
    
    fpath.list <- list.files(file.root_path, 
                             full.names = TRUE)
    
    fpath.len <- length(fpath.list)

    # If the number of files is limited and 
    # the total number of files in the folder exceeds the limit
    if(!is.na(char_files.max) && fpath.len > char_files.max){
      
      # If a seed is provided.
      if (!is.na(seed)) {
        #' Applies a reproducibility seed offset 
        #' by the folder's index
        set.seed(seed + folder.idx)
      }
      
      
      if(random_sample) {
        # Samples the files randomly
        file.idx <- sample(fpath.len, size = char_files.max)
      } else {
        #' Selects the `char_files.max` top files 
        #' according to the specified limit.
        file.idx <- seq_len(char_files.max)
      }
      
      fpath.list <- fpath.list[file.idx]
    }
    
    list(root_path = file.root_path,
         file_path.list = fpath.list)
  })
  
  #' Shortens the name of each list item to the first character 
  #' of the folder name..
  names(path_list) <- folder.list |> substr(1,1)
  path_list
}
```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
The complete version of the [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) is available in the [Data Loading](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L-L) Section of the [data.helper.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) script on _GitHub_.
:::

#### [load.img_trimmed.dat](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L) Function {#func.load.img_trimmed.dat}
\

This specialized utility function reads an image file, dynamically detects whether it contains nonzero pixel data, optionally trims whitespace or empty borders around the visual features using the [magick package](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/index.html), and extracts its raw data matrix structure.

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/ds.train2trimmed_img.dat.R#L12)
\

```{r load.img_trimmed.dat@usage, eval=FALSE}
  train.img_dat.list <- load_image.list(root_path = img.train_root.dir,
                                        fn.load_image.dat = load.img_trimmed.dat
                                        # folder.list = NULL,
                                        # char_files.max = NA,
                                        # seed = NA,
                                        # random_sample = FALSE
                                        )
```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
In the *code snippet* above, a pointer to *this function* is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument to the [load_image.list](#func.load_image.list) function described above in *this Section*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.args.file_path .sidebar }
- **file_path:** Path to the image file to load. 

:::
:::

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. ***Image Loading:*** The function begins by reading the image file from disk into memory as an object using [magick::image_read](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html).

2. ***Matrix Conversion & Validation:*** Converts the loaded image into a numeric matrix representation using the user-defined helper function [magick_img2matrix](#func.magick_img2matrix) described below in described below in the [Image Processing](#appndx_a@img_proc) Section.

3. ***Image Validation & Conditional Cropping:*** Evaluates the matrix's maximum value to check whether the image is entirely blank or empty. If valid content exists (the maximum pixel value is greater than zero), it applies [magick::image_trim](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html) to automatically crop out uniform background borders or whitespace, centering the content around the core visual features.

4. ***Data Extraction:*** Finally, it extracts and returns the underlying raw pixel buffer data using the [magick::image_data](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details) helper function.

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
This is an auxiliary function, the pointer to which is passed in the [fn.load_image.dat](#func.load_image.list.args.fn.load_image.dat) argument to the [load_image.list](#func.load_image.list) function, as shown above in the [Usage](#func.load.img_trimmed.dat.usage) Section of *this Description*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.value .sidebar }
##### Value
\

Raw pixel buffer data from the trimmed image, returned by the internal call to [magick::image_data](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details).
:::

\newpage

::: { #func.load.img_trimmed.dat.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L287) of the function is shown below:
```{r func@load.img_trimmed.dat.s, eval=FALSE}
load.img_trimmed.dat <- function(file_path) {
  # Reads the image file from disk
  img <- magick::image_read(file_path)
  
  # Converts the loaded image into a numeric matrix representation
  img.mx <- magick_img2matrix(img)
  
  img.trimmed <- img

  #' Evaluates the matrix's maximum value to check 
  #' whether the image is entirely blank or empty.
  if (max(img.mx) > 0) {
    img.trimmed <- image_trim(img)
  }
  
  # Extracts and returns the underlying raw pixel buffer data.
  magick::image_data(img.trimmed)
}

```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
During the execution, it calls internally the user-defined helper function [magick_img2matrix](#func.magick_img2matrix) described below in Section [Image Processing](#appndx_a.img_proc) of [Appendix A](#appndx_a) of *this Report*.
:::
:::

\newpage

### Image Processing {#appndx_a.img_proc}

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
The complete source code of the functions described in this Section is available in the [Image Processing](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/tree/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L420-L488) Section of the [data-helper.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/tree/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L420-L488) script on _GitHub_.
:::

#### [magick_img2matrix](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L485) Function {#func.magick_img2matrix}
\

This is a lightweight utility that converts a [***magick** image* object](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details) into a *normalized numeric matrix of pixel intensities*.


::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.usage .sidebar }
##### [Usage](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L)
\

```{r dmagick_img2matrix@usage.setup, eval=TRUE}
# Sample image file:
file_path <- "../../data/raw/Vaibs.HW-Chars/Train/W/0.jpg"
img <- magick::image_read(file_path)
```
```{r dmagick_img2matrix@usage.before_proc, echo=FALSE}
writeLines("*** Image visualization before processing ***")
```
```{r dmagick_img2matrix@usage.plot_before, echo=TRUE}
# Reads the image file from disk
plot(img)

```

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
In the *code snippet* below, *this function* is called internally from the [load.img_trimmed.dat](#func.load.img_trimmed.dat) function described above in Section [Data Loading](#appndx_a.dat_load).
:::

```{r dmagick_img2matrix@usage.proc, echo=TRUE}
# Converts the loaded image into a numeric matrix representation
img.mx <- magick_img2matrix(img)
```
```{r dmagick_img2matrix@usage.after_proc, echo=FALSE}
writeLines("*** Image data view after processing ***")
```
```{r dmagick_img2matrix@usage.data_view, echo=TRUE}
str(img.mx)
image.mx(img.mx)
```
```{r dmagick_img2matrix@usage.cleanup, include=FALSE}
rm(file_path,
   img,
   img.mx)
```
:::

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.args .sidebar }
##### Arguments
\

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.args.img .sidebar }
- **img:** A [Magick Image object](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details) (typically processed, resized, or filtered prior to conversion). 

:::
:::

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.details .sidebar }
##### Details
\

Below is the *step-by-step execution flow* of the function:

1. ***Raw Binary Data Extraction:*** The function calls the [image_data] function to extract the underlying raw hexadecimal or integer byte array buffer from the [*magick* Image object](https://docs.ropensci.org/magick/reference/editing.html#details).
2. ***Color Channel Isolation:*** Slices the multidimensional array to isolate the primary color channel matrix. For grayscale or black-and-white pipeline images (as in our case), this captures the single intensity plane.
3. ***Data Type Conversion:*** Explicitly casts the extracted data array elements from raw/character bytes into a numeric data type, making mathematical operations possible.
4. ***Min-Max Normalization:*** Divides the entire matrix by 255 (the maximum 8-bit color intensity value) to normalize pixel values into a clean floating-point scale ranging from 0.0 (black/background) to 1.0 

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
This is a utility function used internally by the other user-defined functions, as shown in the usage example above in the [Usage](#func.magick_img2matrix.usage) Section of *this Description*.
:::
:::

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.value .sidebar }
##### Value
\

*Grayscale image* data matrix representing *pixel intensity*, normalized to a *floating-point* scale ranging from $0.0$ (black/background) to $1.0$.

:::

::: { #func.magick_img2matrix.code .sidebar }
##### Source Code
\

The [source code](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-functions/data-helper.R#L485) of the function is shown below:
```{r src@magick_img2matrix, eval=FALSE}
magick_img2matrix <- function(img){
  #' Extract the underlying raw byte array buffer 
  #' from the `magick` image object.
  img.dat <- image_data(img)
  
  #' Slice the multidimensional array to isolate 
  #' the primary color channel matrix (capture the single intensity plane).
  mx.bin <- img.dat[1,,]
  
  #' Cast the extracted data array elements from raw/character bytes 
  #' into a numeric data type.
  mode(mx.bin) <- "numeric"
  
  #' Normalize pixel values into a clean floating-point scale 
  #' ranging from 0.0 (black/background) to 1.0. 
  mx.bin /255
}

```

:::
